Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide on-grid invariant

## Summary
Replace the hard-coded fire-rate constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` with values derived from the 80 BPM beat period. Each weapon fires at an exact subdivision: cannon 2/beat (375 ms), spread 1/beat (750 ms), dual 1/beat (750 ms), rapid 6/beat (125 ms). Add a catalogue-wide test asserting every fire rate divides evenly into the beat period.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — All `WEAPON_*_FIRE_RATE` constants in `src/utils/weapons.ts` become derived from the beat period (e.g. `beatPeriodMs / subdivisions`), not hard-coded literals.
- [ ] **AC2** — `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` fire rates match the producer-specified values: cannon 375 ms (2/beat), spread 750 ms (1/beat), dual 750 ms (1/beat), rapid 125 ms (6/beat).
- [ ] **AC3** — A catalogue-wide invariant test asserts `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` for every weapon in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`.
- [ ] **AC4** — Existing weapon tests still pass after the refactor (no behaviour change beyond timing).
- [ ] **AC5** — New weapons added to the catalogue must satisfy the invariant; the test fails if they do not.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC3** — [ ] **AC3 — Per-weapon subdivisions + catalogue-wide invariant.** Each weapon's fire interval is an exact subdivision of the beat: **cannon 375 ms (160 BPM, 2/beat)**, **spread 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **dual 750 ms (80 BPM, 1/beat)**, **rapid 125 ms (480 BPM, 6/beat)**. A catalogue-wide test asserts every `WeaponDefinition.fireRateMs` satisfies `beatPeriodMs % fireRateMs === 0` (equivalently `fireRateMs × n === beatPeriodMs` for a positive integer `n`), so the future 20 BPM quarter-time weapon and any other new weapon are on-grid by construction.

## Key Files
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — fire rates derived from beat period.
- `src/utils/weapons.test.ts` — invariant test.

## Risks
- Low: existing tests will verify no unintended behaviour changes. The rapid weapon (125 ms) is unchanged; cannon, spread, and dual rates change slightly.
data.title: Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant

Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

## Summary
Replace the independent per-weapon cooldown model in `Player.tryFire` with phase-locked scheduling on the shared beat clock. A weapons next shot time is the smallest multiple of its interval at/after the current beat-clock time. Collection may delay the first shot to the next grid tick (by design). All active weapons share the same anchor so they stay phase-locked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1** — `Player.tryFire(dt)` no longer uses independent per-weapon cooldowns — every shot is snapped to the shared beat clock.
- [ ] **AC2** — All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns).
- [ ] **AC3** — A weapon collected mid-beat fires its first shot on the next grid tick (by design).
- [ ] **AC4** — Cumulative and timed weapon semantics are unchanged (collection, expiry, reset all work as before).
- [ ] **AC5** — Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick, verified with multiple active weapons.
- [ ] **Traces to parent AC2** — [ ] **AC2 — All player fire is globally quantised.** Player auto-fire (`Player.tryFire` and its callers in `CombatScene`/`GymWeapons`) emits shots only on ticks of the shared beat clock, phase-locked to the scene/beat anchor — never off-grid — regardless of when a weapon is collected or the frame rate. All simultaneously active weapons fire on the same shared grid (no independent, drifting cooldowns). Tests assert every emitted shot time is an exact grid tick.

## Key Files
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `tryFire` / cooldown model → phase-locked scheduling.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — grid-tick emission tests.

## Risks
- Medium: this changes the core fire model. Must preserve cumulative/timed weapon semantics. Tests must verify phase-locking with multiple active weapons.
data.title: Replace Player.tryFire per-weapon cooldowns with phase-locked beat scheduling

# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Intake Brief — When ships explode when a level times out we need major SFX explosion (AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC)

## Headline

Add a new dedicated, layered "major explosion" SFX to the wave-timeout path,
played once per detonating ship (with a concurrency/rate limiter), so the 10×
detonation of surviving enemies is no longer silent.

## Problem statement

When a wave times out, every surviving non-asteroid enemy detonates at 10×
scale (`WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE`), but no explosion sound plays for those
detonations. The only audio on the timeout path is the generic player
life-loss cue (`playDestructionSound()` via `_loseLife(false)`), so the
dramatic 10× visual blast lands silently and the moment reads as flat.

## Users

- **Player** — the wave-timeout wipe should be audible as a major explosion,
  making the lost life and the 10× detonation feel consequential.
- **Developer / designer tuning feel** — one place (exported constants) to tune
  the cue's layering, volume, duration and voice cap.

### Example user story

- As a **player**, when the level timer hits zero and my remaining enemies
  detonate, I hear a large, heavy explosion cue so the moment reads as a major
  event rather than a silent animation.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()` detonates every non-asteroid
  survivor via `s.entity.destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)` and calls
  `_loseLife(false)`; it plays **no SFX for the detonations**.
  `WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE = 10`.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `destroySelf(scale)` → `playExplosion(scale)`
  only spawns particles; the class comment states audio is played by the scene
  at destruction time.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playDestructionSound()` (generic 440→60 Hz
  sawtooth pop) and the layered `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (impact thump +
  descending body + noise tail). No "major" or timeout-specific cue exists.
- GDD §7.3 documents the two existing cues and states "the wave-timeout life
  penalty and shield absorption keep the generic cue". It also flags the risk
  "SFX rate limiting — … avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX
  instances".
- Tests live in `src/audio/effects.test.ts`, `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts`
  and `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`.

## Desired change

Add a new dedicated, layered `playMajorExplosionSound()` cue in
`src/audio/effects.ts` and wire it into `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` so it fires
once per detonating ship, guarded by a concurrency/rate limiter so stacked cues
stay within the GDD §7.3 audio ceiling. Document the new cue in GDD §7.3 and
cover it with automated tests.

## Producer decisions (recorded)

- **Q1 — Blast granularity: B** → one heavy cue **per detonating ship**, with
  attenuation/rate-limiting.
- **Q2 — Cue identity: A** → a **new dedicated** `playMajorExplosionSound()`,
  not a reuse of `playPlayerDestructionSound()`.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout: A** → keep the **generic**
  `playDestructionSound()` for the player's timeout life loss; only the enemy
  detonations get the major blast cue.

## Assumptions

1. The limiter caps concurrent major-explosion voices at an exported
   `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` (default aligned to the GDD's "≤ 3–4 concurrent
   SFX" guidance); triggers beyond the cap are coalesced/attenuated rather than
   stacking at full gain. [ASSUMPTION]
2. Scope is audio only — the 10× particle blast already exists, so no new VFX.
   [ASSUMPTION]
3. `PlayScene` is the only wave-timeout path (no gym scene has a wave timeout),
   so wiring is confined to `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`. [ASSUMPTION]
4. The cue routes through the existing SFX master gain/mute plumbing and is a
   safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests, autoplay-blocked
   browsers). [ASSUMPTION]

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()` is defined in
   `src/audio/effects.ts` using layered procedural synthesis (impact thump +
   descending body + noise tail), with every amplitude, duration and voice-cap
   value exposed as an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant; the cue is
   documented in GDD §7.3.
2. When a wave/level times out with surviving non-asteroid enemies, the major
   explosion cue is triggered **once per detonating ship** (verified by a
   `PlayScene` test whose spy count equals the number of detonated survivors).
3. A concurrency/rate limiter keeps stacked per-ship cues within the GDD §7.3
   audio ceiling: no more than `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` concurrent
   major-explosion voices, with excess triggers attenuated/coalesced — verified
   by unit tests that exercise many simultaneous triggers.
4. When a wave/level times out with no enemies remaining, no major-explosion
   cue plays and the player's generic life-loss cue is unchanged (no
   `playPlayerDestructionSound()` on this path) — verified by tests.
5. The cue routes through the SFX master volume/mute and is a safe no-op
   without an `AudioContext` — verified by tests.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- All SFX remain **procedural** (Web Audio API, zero external audio assets) per
  GDD §7.3.
- Respect the GDD §7.3 ceiling and the "avoid stacking more than 3–4 concurrent
  SFX instances" risk mitigation.
- No new gameplay behaviour: the timeout detonation/one-life penalty is
  unchanged; this is feedback only.
- No new VFX.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playMajorExplosionSound()` and its
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` tuning/limiter constants (mirroring the layered
  `playPlayerDestructionSound()` structure).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Call the new cue once per detonating ship in
  `_timeoutWave()` (alongside `destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)`);
  leave `_loseLife(false)` and its generic cue untouched.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` / `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — Unit tests
  for layering, limiter/voice cap, master volume/mute routing and
  no-AudioContext no-op.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — Timeout wiring tests (one cue per ship, none
  when no enemies, generic player cue unchanged).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 SFX event catalog and player audio
  character section: document the new major-explosion cue and its limiter.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Limiter tuning may need an audio playtest.** Whether the per-ship stack
  reads as one "major" blast or as mud cannot be judged from unit tests alone;
  `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` and per-voice gain are exported for tuning.
  [Medium]
- **Masking/clipping risk.** Many near-simultaneous heavy cues could mask
  other SFX or clip; mitigated by the voice cap/attenuation (GDD §7.3 "avoid
  stacking more than 3–4 concurrent SFX instances"). [Medium]
- **Browser autoplay policy.** The cue stays silent until a user gesture
  starts the `AudioContext`; it must remain a safe no-op when no context
  exists. [Low]
- **Scope-creep guard.** Reusing the new major cue for other events (boss
  death, P4 bomb clear, player death) is out of scope; record those as linked
  work items rather than widening this item. [Low]
- **Assumption:** no gym wave-timeout path exists today; if one is added
  later, it must reuse the same cue + limiter rather than duplicating it.
  [Low]

## Related work

- AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6 — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x
  scale and cost a life (added the timeout detonation; completed).
- AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L — Asteroids should not explode when time runs out,
  instead carry them over (completed).
- AH-0MUAYB4R3002ZIZY — Need juice when the player is destroyed (precedent for
  a dedicated layered cue; completed).
- AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A — dedicated player-destruction cue (implemented
  `playPlayerDestructionSound`).
- AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V — Add particle-based explosion VFX for enemy and player
  deaths (completed).
- AH-0MU0AVBWH002ZWRH — Add randomness to explosion (completed).
- AH-0MUA8B6MT006M1KS — SFX master volume + mute plumbing in effects.ts
  (completed).
- AH-0MUA8BEUR006RWCI — SettingsScene: SFX volume slider + mute toggle
  (completed).
- AH-0MU3VPIA900697E8 — Ensure all enemies have SFX on their fire event
  (completed).
- AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1 — Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD
  (completed).

## Related work (automated report)

> Generated by the `find-related` skill. Conservative ranking; treat as
> suggestions, not a complete list.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUBYXR280018HST** – PlayScene: wire absorb animation + pop SFX into collection path (completed)
- **AH-0MTFU1GAO009KDBM** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52** – Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: absorption, ac3, acceptance, add, added (+200 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absorption, ac3, add, added, also (+199 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, added, already, also, animation (+160 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Blast granularity: Should the "major SFX explosion" be one cue per
  timeout event, or one cue per detonating ship?** — Answer (producer, via
  interactive reply): **B) one heavy cue per detonating ship, with
  attenuation/rate-limiting.** Agent recommendation had been A (single cue);
  producer chose B, so a limiter is now an explicit AC. Final accepted answer:
  B.
- **Q2 — Cue identity: Should this be a new dedicated cue or a reuse of an
  existing one?** — Answer (producer, via interactive reply): **A) a new
  dedicated `playMajorExplosionSound()`.** Final accepted answer: A.
- **Q3 — Player life-loss cue on timeout: upgrade to the heavy
  player-destruction cue, or only the enemy detonations?** — Answer (producer,
  via interactive reply): **A) keep the generic player life-loss cue and add
  only the blast cue.** Final accepted answer: A.
data.title: When ships explode when a level times out we need major SFX explosion

parent AC1 (registration/discoverability) and the gym half of AC6. Fifth
feature in the plan's dependency order (F1 → F8).

## Goal

Make the Harvester a **rare roaming spawn in later levels (Levels 4–5)** using
a dedicated later-level spawner, registered with the `WaveManager` so
wave-clear accounting stays correct.

Part of **Harvester enemy (AH-0MUI820PM0038HS2)**, feature **F6**. Covers
parent AC6 (campaign integration). Sixth feature in the plan's dependency order
(F1 → F8).

## Producer decision (2026-09-27)

- **Integration mechanism = option (a):** a dedicated later-level roaming
  spawner modelled on `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts`, invoked by `PlayScene`
  for Levels 4–5 and registered via `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn`. This
  works identically for the static and the data-driven sequenced campaign and
  keeps Levels 1–3 clean.
- **Candidate pool:** `harvester` is deliberately **excluded** from
  `defaultCandidatePool()` (`src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`) so the
  difficulty auto-sequencer cannot select it at any level.

## User story

As a player, I want the Harvester to appear rarely in the harder levels, so it
is a memorable mineral-denial threat rather than constant noise.

## Scope

- New pure planner (e.g. `src/waves/HarvesterSpawner.ts`) modelled on
  `AsteroidSpawner.ts`, with unit tests.
- `PlayScene` release path gated to Levels 4–5, with each spawn registered
  through `WaveManager.registerDynamicSpawn`.
- Disable Harvester spawns in the boss encounter and in Levels 1–3.
- Ensure `defaultCandidatePool()` omits `harvester`, pinned by a test.
- Wave/level test for accounting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Harvester spawns occur only in Levels 4–5, are rare (bounded per wave), and
  never occur in the boss encounter.
- Every Harvester spawn is registered with the `WaveManager` so the wave
  neither clears early nor stalls; a wave/level test verifies the accounting.
- The data-driven sequenced campaign and the static campaign both exhibit the
  same later-level behaviour.
- `defaultCandidatePool()` does not include `harvester`, pinned by a test.
- Campaign integration (AC6): the Harvester is available in the gym and in
  later levels.

## Depends on

- F5 (Harvester archetype registration and gym exposure)

## Key Files

- `src/waves/HarvesterSpawner.ts` (new) + `src/waves/HarvesterSpawner.test.ts`
- `src/waves/AsteroidSpawner.ts` (reference)
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`

## Constraints

- Scope is a rare roaming spawn in Levels 4–5 only — no wave/level redesign.
- UK English in all written output.

# Tests: asteroid-independent wave completion and persistence

Parent: AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO (bug, high).

## Goal / User story

As a tester, I want deterministic tests that assert a wave completes as soon as
the enemy ships are gone (regardless of live asteroids), and that asteroids and
minerals persist across wave/level transitions, so the new wave rule cannot
silently regress.

This is the **test-first** work item for the parent bug: write/adjust the tests
so they encode the new rule and fail (red) against the current, old-rule code.

## Scope

Update the tests that currently assert the old rule and add new coverage:

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`:
  - Replace `AC6 — the wave clears only after ALL split children are destroyed`.
  - Replace `AH-0MU8TWF1H007OG2L AC5 — carried-over asteroids are re-registered…`.
  - Update the asteroid-integration accounting assertions that expect a split
    child / released asteroid to increment `enemiesAlive` (approx. lines 1232,
    1257).
  - Update the asteroid-spawner integration assertion that a released asteroid
    increments `enemiesAlive` (approx. lines 2327, 2349).
  - Add: wave clears with live asteroids present; `enemiesAlive` excludes
    asteroids and split children; asteroids persist across a wave transition
    and across a level transition; timeout does not re-register asteroids;
    minerals persist across a transition; boss-entry clearing still destroys
    carried-over asteroids.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts`: re-frame the "dynamic spawn registration"
  suite as the generic seam (drop the asteroid-semantics claim); keep the API
  tests, because the API is retained.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Wave completion ignores asteroids — test: the wave clears while non-asteroid
  enemy ships are destroyed even when asteroids remain alive, and
  `WaveManager.enemiesAlive` excludes them.
- Minerals persist — test: minerals already on the field remain in place across
  wave and level transitions.
- Boss entry keeps clearing asteroids — test: carried-over asteroids are still
  destroyed when the boss encounter begins.
- Tests updated and comprehensive — unit/integration tests cover wave clearing
  with live asteroids, `enemiesAlive` excluding asteroids and split children,
  persistence across wave and level transitions, and timeout not re-registering
  asteroids.
- A test asserts a released offscreen asteroid and a split child do not
  increment `WaveManager.enemiesAlive`.
- A test asserts surviving asteroids remain alive and continue to move after a
  wave transition and after a level transition.
- A test asserts a surviving asteroid is not re-registered on wave timeout (for
  example, `enemiesAlive` after timeout equals the next wave's enemy-ship
  count).
- All added/updated tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no wall-clock waits)
  and fail (red) against the pre-change code.
- The rest of the suite still runs with no unrelated failures; the new/updated
  tests fail only on the old-rule assertions.

## Minimal Implementation

- Use the existing PlayScene test harness helpers (`findAsteroids`, the
  `wm` accessor, the wave-timeout helper).
- Assert directly on `WaveManager.enemiesAlive` and scene alive counts; avoid
  timing-based waits.
- Title replaced tests with the parent id, e.g.
  `AH-0MUJM746P000QAEO AC1 — wave clears with live asteroids`.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — replace/extend the wave-accounting and persistence tests.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.test.ts` — re-frame the dynamic-spawn suite.

## Dependencies

- None (first item).

## Deliverables

- Red (failing) tests encoding the new rule.
- A comment listing every replaced/added test.

## Verification

- `npm test -- --run` (the repo's standard vitest invocation) shows the new
  tests failing only on the old-rule assertions.

# Major-explosion SFX regression sweep

## Goal
Verify the wave-timeout major-explosion SFX end-to-end: the full suite passes with the new cue, voice limiter and `PlayScene` wiring, and no path double-plays the major cue with the generic or player-destruction cue.

## User story
As a developer, I want a regression sweep that proves the new timeout cue is safe (no double-play, no clipping regression, full suite green) so I can ship the change with confidence.

## Scope
- Run the full project test suite and checks with the new cue, limiter and wiring in place.
- Verify the wave-timeout path does not double-play the major cue alongside the generic life-loss cue or the player-destruction cue.
- Confirm gym↔game parity: no gym wave-timeout path exists today; if one is added later it must reuse the same cue + limiter (record as a follow-up, do not modify gyms here).
- Confirm the repo-wide duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes.

## Test-first ordering
This verification item is created before the implementation items (per the plan skill's test-first ordering rule). It depends on them, so it runs last.

## Constraints
- Verification only: no production behaviour change in this item.
- If a regression is found, record it as a linked `test-failure` work item rather than widening this item.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC (AC7); `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_timeoutWave()`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (gym↔game duplicate-body guard).
- GDD §7.3 Audio Direction; AGENTS.md gym↔game parity convention.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Full project test suite (`npm test`) passes with the new cue, limiter and PlayScene wiring.
- `npm run typecheck` and the build pass.
- Cross-path check: no scenario double-plays the major cue with the generic `playDestructionSound()` or `playPlayerDestructionSound()` on the wave-timeout path.
- Gym↔game parity confirmed: no gym wave-timeout path exists; any future gym timeout reuses the same cue + limiter (documented as a follow-up).
- The repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` passes.
- Covers parent AC7.

# Per-wave generation modes: curve-fixed, hand-authored fixed and dynamic runtime regeneration

## Goal

As a **designer**, I want to mark each configured wave with a **generation mode**, so one campaign can mix hand-authored set-pieces with curve-driven and runtime-regenerated waves.

Three modes (the default is (a)):

- **(a) `curve` — curve-generated, fixed at runtime.** The sequencer builds the wave from its `targetDifficulty` once; the composition is then fixed for the whole run. It only changes when the designer explicitly asks for a level/wave regeneration (the `Regenerate` action).
- **(b) `fixed` — hand-authored, never regenerated.** The wave composition is authored and used verbatim at design and runtime. It is never passed through the sequencer. Its difficulty is *derived* from its settings (shown read-only in the editor — see sibling item 2).
- **(c) `dynamic` — regenerated at runtime.** The wave is rebuilt from its curve by the sequencer at runtime, seeded from the run's RNG, so successive runs differ while remaining reproducible for a given seed.

## Context / existing state

- `DifficultyCurveRow` — `src/core/configTypes.ts:88` — currently `level`, `levelName`, `wave`, `targetDifficulty`.
- Codec/validation — `src/core/csv.ts:405` (`DIFFICULTY_CURVE_COLUMN_ORDER`, `parseDifficultyCurves`, `serializeDifficultyCurves`, `validateDifficultyCurveRow`) and the Vite dev writer `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts`.
- Seeded config — `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`.
- Builder — `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` (`buildSequencedLevels`), currently pure/deterministic and always curve-generated.
- Runtime wiring — `resolveCampaignLevels`/`PlayScene.create` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:202,405`) and `WaveManager.setLevels` (`src/waves/WaveManager.ts:103`).
- Editor preview — `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.

## Relationships

- **Supersedes / generalises Support mixed generated and scripted levels in a campaign (AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD)** to per-wave granularity and adds the `dynamic` mode. Reconcile at intake: preferred outcome is that this item absorbs that scope and AH-0MUH7Q6HN0006QPD is closed as superseded or reduced to any residual per-level behaviour.
- Enables the sibling UI item (generation-mode control in the curve generator) and the default-on item.

## Desired behaviour

- Add a `generation` column (`curve` | `fixed` | `dynamic`) to `DifficultyCurveRow`, the codec (`DIFFICULTY_CURVE_COLUMN_ORDER`, parse/serialize/validate), the Vite plugin whitelist and the seed CSV. An **absent** value means `curve`, so existing 4-column files and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` keep working unchanged.
- The builder honours the mode per wave:
  - `curve`: unchanged — one sequencer call per level, composition fixed for the run.
  - `fixed`: use the hand-authored composition verbatim; **never** call the sequencer for that wave.
  - `dynamic`: call the sequencer at wave-build time using an injectable run seed/RNG so the wave differs between runs but is reproducible for a given seed.
- Determinism contract: `curve` and `fixed` waves are independent of the seed; `dynamic` waves are a pure function of (curve, candidate pool, seed).
- Fallback: missing/unknown mode ⇒ `curve`; a malformed mode is treated like any other malformed row (dropped, existing file-level default-curve fallback preserved). A `fixed` wave whose composition cannot be resolved must fall back safely, never crash the run.
- **Open decision (resolve at intake):** where a `fixed` wave's composition is stored. Preferred: reuse the hand-authored static `LEVELS` wave for the same level/wave number. Alternative: persist an explicit serialized composition (groups) in the campaign config. Document whichever is chosen, including behaviour for levels numbered beyond `LEVEL_COUNT`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The generation-mode column round-trips: `parseDifficultyCurves(serializeDifficultyCurves(rows))` preserves each wave's mode.
- Absent mode defaults to `curve`; existing 4-column CSV rows and `defaultDifficultyCurves()` output are unchanged.
- `fixed` waves are never passed to the sequencer (assertable via a spy/injected sequencer) and match their authored composition exactly.
- `dynamic` waves differ between at least two distinct seeds, and are identical for the same seed (test asserts both).
- `curve` and `fixed` waves are identical regardless of seed.
- Malformed/unknown mode rows and unresolvable `fixed` waves degrade safely (no crash; campaign remains playable).
- The Vite dev writer accepts valid `generation` values and rejects an invalid value with HTTP 400.
- Documentation (README, GDD, design doc and module comments) describes the three modes, the default and the seed/RNG contract for `dynamic`.
- New unit/integration tests cover the codec, mode dispatch, seed determinism and `fixed` sourcing; the full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add `generation` to `DifficultyCurveRow`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend the difficulty-curve codec/validator.
- `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — whitelist/validate the new column.
- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — add the column to the seed config.
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — mode dispatch, seed threading and `fixed` sourcing.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `defaultDifficultyCurves()` mode defaults.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — thread the run seed into the builder for `dynamic` waves.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — verify injection seam; minimal change expected.
- Tests: `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/waves/sequencedLevels.test.ts`, `src/core/configStore.test.ts`.

data.description: Follow-up (discovered-from:AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC). No gym scene currently has a wave timer/timeout, so the wave-timeout major-explosion SFX (`playMajorExplosionSound()` + its concurrency limiter) is implemented only on `PlayScene._timeoutWave()`. Per the gym↔game parity convention (AGENTS.md), if a gym ever gains a wave-timeout path it MUST call the same `playMajorExplosionSound()` (and inherit its limiter) rather than duplicating the cue. This item is a placeholder to keep that parity obligation visible; no code change is required today. Acceptance criteria: a gym wave-timeout (if introduced) plays the shared major-explosion cue with the same voice cap and constants, with a parity test.
